root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `*tmp != '\0'` immediately after `tmp++` on the escape path.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `unescape_tag()` consumes a backslash escape by executing `tmp++`, the resulting escape target must be a real character, not the string terminator. If `tmp++` lands on `\0`, the function must stop before the loop epilogue advances `tmp` into the next loop-condition read.
root_cause_criterion.description: On the saved PoC's final lone backslash, vulnerable `unescape_tag()` increments `tmp` onto the `kv[1]` terminator and continues. The fixed program adds `if (*tmp == '\0') break;` at this exact point, so the same input is guarded before the next `*tmp != '\0'` evaluation.

nodes.state: The next evaluation of `*tmp != '\0'` at line 395 reads through the same `tmp` pointer produced by the prior loop epilogue. Because the root step already showed that the prior pointer was the terminator and the epilogue advanced beyond it, this is the AddressSanitizer-reported one-byte read past `kv[1]`.

After the vulnerable final escape iteration continues with `*tmp == '\0'`, the line-395 loop epilogue advances `tmp` past that terminator, leaving the next condition pointer one byte beyond the tag string.

edges.relation: Once the lone trailing escape increments `tmp` onto `kv[1]`'s terminator, the same vulnerable iteration still executes the line-395 loop epilogue, so the next condition pointer becomes strictly greater than that terminator pointer.
The exact pointer value produced by the vulnerable loop epilogue is the `tmp` pointer read by the next `*tmp != '\0'` condition check.
